newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New charges for Dutroux in Belgian child sex case.
newsitem.headline: New charges for Dutroux in Belgian child sex case.

text.p: Belgian authorities said they were charging Marc Dutroux, the chief suspect in the country's child sex, murder and kidnap scandal in which four young girls died, with three new crimes.

Public prosecutors in the southern town of Neufchateau said in a statement Dutroux, a convicted child rapist, was now formally being accused of the illegal incarceration and the murder of the girls An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks.
The rapes of Sabine Dardenne and Laetitia Delhez have also been added to the charge sheet, their office said, and formal arrest warrants related to the charges were issued against Dutroux.

Previously, Dutroux had been charged with criminal association, the murder of Bernard Weinstein, one of his accomplices, kidnapping and illegally locking up Dardenne and Delhez, and theft and trafficking in stolen cars.
Belgian radio said the new warrants meant Dutroux was very unlikely to be released from detention -- he was arrested in the summer of last year -- in the runup to his trial.
No start date has been set for trial proceedings as investigators continue their search for bodies of other missing girls, suspected to have fallen victim to the Dutroux gang.
The radio said the new charges were brought after pressure from a court in Liege on the prosecutors to charge Dutroux with all the crimes they had evidence for.
Marchal and Lambrecks disappeared on the Belgian coast on August 22, 1995, when they were 17 and 19 respectively. Their bodies were found in a house owned by Dutroux early in September of last year.

Dutroux had been arrested in mid-August after a tip-off. Shortly afterwards Dardenne and Delhez were rescued from a secret dungeon in the cellar of a house he owns in the central Belgian city of Charleroi.
Over the next two weeks Dutroux led police to the bodies of four other dead girls, including two eight-year-olds, and that of Weinstein, a Frenchman.

The revelations shocked Belgium and the country reeled in disgust when in the course of the investigation it emerged that police and justice authorities had seriously bungled efforts to find the missing girls.
